question: research/evidence-authority-model/question-v1.0.md
objective: Determine whether a non-self-activating Research candidate evidence-authority contract can satisfy the frozen construction and falsification conditions without claiming Acceptance, Promotion, canonical dependency reconciliation, or experiment authority.

required_checks.name: research_inactivity
required_checks.pass_condition: model registry and manifest are Research inactive and self-activation is prohibited

required_checks.name: external_bootstrap
required_checks.pass_condition: initial Acceptance and Promotion require a preregistered hash-locked authority predating the candidate; absent selection remains Unknown

required_checks.name: governing_dependency_coverage
required_checks.pass_condition: the authority map registers the research-execution charter proof-assurance taxonomy model registry manifest and governance-decision owner with explicit status transitions

required_checks.name: proof_path_completeness
required_checks.pass_condition: independent enumeration covers theorem Markdown proofs lemma proof sources T-001 through T-015 YAML proof objects registered JSON records and registered Lean files

required_checks.name: proof_status_separation
required_checks.pass_condition: ownership pattern alone grants no authority; every registered proof artifact requires one charter status and authority-bearing designation; only authority-bearing Accepted artifacts may carry active proof authority

required_checks.name: manifest_provenance
required_checks.pass_condition: the manifest has a separate top-level acceptance-decision record requirement in addition to per-entry status decisions

required_checks.name: equal_priority_conflict_safety
required_checks.pass_condition: unresolved contradictions at equal or higher priority for the same proposition scope premises and version resolve to Unknown pending governance

required_checks.name: claim_boundary
required_checks.pass_condition: the Research candidate neither authorizes nor prohibits experiments and does not claim Accepted authority dependency derivation theorem truth necessity minimality or universality

falsification_conditions: any candidate artifact can Accept Promote or activate itself
a governing dependency used by the contract is excluded from the authority map
a registered proof path is absent from the proof owner coverage test
a proof artifact can gain active authority without an Accepted charter status and authority-bearing designation
the status manifest can become Accepted without a manifest-level independent decision record
two contradictory equal-priority artifacts can both remain authoritative for the same proposition scope premises and version
the candidate authorizes canonical dependency reconciliation or experiment execution while bootstrap authority remains Unknown

execution_method.source_identity: verify every frozen source blob against frozen_base_commit
execution_method.construction: derive the smallest candidate contract satisfying A1-A8; reject additions not required by a frozen check
execution_method.proof_discovery: parse repository proof metadata and verifier-declared proof-object requirements independently of the candidate owner pattern
execution_method.negative_controls: remove each required governing owner and each proof metadata pathway in turn and require the validation contract to fail
execution_method.conflict_control: inject an equal-priority contradictory proposition and require Unknown rather than dual authority
execution_method.repeat: perform a second clean evaluation from the frozen specification without importing the first result fields

decision_rule.bounded_candidate_supported: all A1-A8 pass and every falsification control is detected
decision_rule.candidate_refuted: at least one A-check fails or at least one falsification control is undetected
decision_rule.unknown: source identity or independent proof-path completeness cannot be verified

lifecycle_constraints.repository_change: limited to Research evidence candidate artifacts and validation wiring

nonclaims: logical derivation of FAR or FARO from FARA
